summary.title: The Cauchy problem for a class of two-dimensional nonlocal nonlinear wave equations governing anti-plane shear motions in elastic materials
summary.authors: H. A. Erbay, S. Erbay, and A. Erkip
summary.executive_summary: This paper analyzes the Cauchy (initial value) problem for a general class of two-dimensional nonlinear nonlocal wave equations that model anti-plane shear motions in nonlocal elastic materials. The nonlocal character of the model is encoded through a convolution integral in the spatial variables, whose Fourier transform is nonnegative and satisfies a growth condition at infinity. The authors establish well-posedness, conditions for global existence, and conditions for finite-time blow-up of solutions for initial data in L2 Sobolev spaces. The central object is the equation w_tt = (β * ∂F/∂w_x)_x + (β * ∂F/∂w_y)_y, where F is a nonlinear function of |∇w|² and β is the convolution kernel. The parameter r in the kernel's Fourier bound controls the regularizing effect of the nonlocal behavior: as r increases, the regularizing effect increases. The paper extends one-dimensional nonlinear nonlocal Boussinesq-type techniques to two dimensions. Local existence is proved for s > 2, and improved to s ≥ 1 when r > 3. Global existence is established under a positivity condition on F together with a growth condition r > 4 and an energy condition. Blow-up is shown to occur in the L∞-norm of |∇w| when the initial energy is negative and a certain inequality on F' holds. The authors note that when β is taken as the Dirac measure, the model reduces to the quasilinear wave equation of conventional elasticity. The work is purely theoretical and contains no numerical experiments, datasets, or computational simulations. The main tools are the Fourier transform, Sobolev embedding, energy conservation, and Gronwall's lemma. The paper is situated within the theory of nonlocal elasticity developed by Kröner, Eringen, Kunin, and others, and it extends prior one-dimensional studies. The results are presented as theorems and lemmas with rigorous proofs, and the paper concludes with an acknowledgement of support from the Scientific and Technological Research Council of Turkey (TUBITAK).

claims.description: The two-dimensional nonlocal wave equation is well-posed locally for sufficiently smooth initial data.
Solutions exist globally in time under a positivity condition on F and a growth condition on the kernel.
Solutions can blow up in finite time when the initial energy is negative.
The nonlocal model reduces to conventional elasticity when the kernel is a Dirac measure.

judge_context:
Executive Summary
This paper analyzes the Cauchy (initial value) problem for a general class of two-dimensional nonlinear nonlocal wave equations that model anti-plane shear motions in nonlocal elastic materials. The nonlocal character of the model is encoded through a convolution integral in the spatial variables, whose Fourier transform is nonnegative and satisfies a growth condition at infinity. The authors establish well-posedness, conditions for global existence, and conditions for finite-time blow-up of solutions for initial data in L2 Sobolev spaces. The central object is the equation w_tt = (β * ∂F/∂w_x)_x + (β * ∂F/∂w_y)_y, where F is a nonlinear function of |∇w|² and β is the convolution kernel. The parameter r in the kernel's Fourier bound controls the regularizing effect of the nonlocal behavior: as r increases, the regularizing effect increases. The paper extends one-dimensional nonlinear nonlocal Boussinesq-type techniques to two dimensions. Local existence is proved for s > 2, and improved to s ≥ 1 when r > 3. Global existence is established under a positivity condition on F together with a growth condition r > 4 and an energy condition. Blow-up is shown to occur in the L∞-norm of |∇w| when the initial energy is negative and a certain inequality on F' holds. The authors note that when β is taken as the Dirac measure, the model reduces to the quasilinear wave equation of conventional elasticity. The work is purely theoretical and contains no numerical experiments, datasets, or computational simulations. The main tools are the Fourier transform, Sobolev embedding, energy conservation, and Gronwall's lemma. The paper is situated within the theory of nonlocal elasticity developed by Kröner, Eringen, Kunin, and others, and it extends prior one-dimensional studies. The results are presented as theorems and lemmas with rigorous proofs, and the paper concludes with an acknowledgement of support from the Scientific and Technological Research Council of Turkey (TUBITAK).

Research Context
Conventional elasticity lacks an intrinsic length scale. Conventional theory fails at small scales and crack tips. Nonlocal elasticity lets stress depend on the whole strain field. Prior work focused on one-dimensional nonlinear nonlocal models. Most nonlocal elasticity research concerns linear models. The number r governs the regularizing effect of nonlocality.

Research Question And Hypothesis
The paper aims to establish well-posedness, global existence, and blow-up. The model captures anti-plane shear in nonlinear nonlocal elasticity. The kernel's Fourier transform must be nonnegative with a growth bound. Larger r strengthens the regularizing effect of the kernel. Local existence is expected for sufficiently smooth initial data. Global existence is expected under a positivity condition on F. Finite-time blow-up is expected for negative initial energy. The Dirac-measure kernel recovers conventional elasticity.

Methodological Details
The study is a purely theoretical mathematical analysis. No participants, samples, or experimental subjects are involved. The governing equation is a two-dimensional nonlocal wave equation. F is a nonlinear function of the squared gradient magnitude. The convolution kernel is defined via a two-dimensional integral. The kernel's Fourier transform satisfies a nonnegativity and growth bound. The constant C is positive and r is at least 2. Initial data are prescribed in L2 Sobolev spaces. The Banach space Xs combines Sobolev and L∞ regularity. The Xs norm aggregates the Hs norm and gradient L∞ norms. The Fourier transform and inverse transform are defined explicitly. The Hs norm uses the Fourier representation.

Procedures And Architectures
Local well-posedness converts the PDE into an ODE system. The system pairs w with its time derivative v. The operator K encodes the convolution and nonlinear gradient terms. Sobolev embedding is used to control the gradient in L∞. Local existence requires s > 2. The operator K is shown to be locally Lipschitz on Xs. Higher regularity improves the local existence threshold. Global existence uses a linear operator R built from the kernel. Energy conservation is established via Parseval's identity. Global existence requires r > 4 and a positivity condition on F. Gronwall's lemma bounds the solution norms. Blow-up is characterized in the L∞-norm of the gradient.

Key Results
Local well-posedness holds for s > 2 and r ≥ 2. Local well-posedness improves to s ≥ 1 when r > 3. Blow-up is characterized by the gradient L∞ norm diverging. Global existence requires r > 4 and a positivity condition on F. Global existence requires the initial energy to be controlled. A lower bound on F guarantees global existence. Blow-up occurs in finite time for negative initial energy. Blow-up requires a growth inequality on F'. The blow-up function H satisfies a differential inequality. The blow-up time is bounded by the initial data. Blow-up may occur even for small initial data. The Dirac-measure kernel recovers conventional elasticity.

Interpretation And Theoretical Implications
The parameter r quantifies the regularizing effect of nonlocality. Higher smoothness of the kernel permits lower Sobolev regularity. The nonlocal model reduces to conventional elasticity. Energy conservation underpins the global existence proof. Negative energy is the mechanism enabling finite-time blow-up. The results extend one-dimensional nonlocal techniques. The framework generalizes to F(wx, wy)-type nonlinearities.

Contradictions And Limitations
The positivity condition is required for global existence. The growth condition r > 4 is required for global existence. The blow-up condition requires negative initial energy. The analysis assumes sufficient smoothness of initial data. The kernel's Fourier transform must satisfy a growth bound. The omission is important because the study is theoretical.

Claims
The two-dimensional nonlocal wave equation is well-posed locally for sufficiently smooth initial data. Local well-posedness holds for s > 2. The operator K is locally Lipschitz. The solution lies in a continuous function space. Higher regularity is needed for lower Sobolev thresholds. The result extends one-dimensional techniques.
Solutions exist globally in time under a positivity condition on F and a growth condition on the kernel. Global existence requires r > 4. A positivity condition on F is required. Energy conservation is used. Negative energy leads to blow-up instead. The result depends on the sign of the initial energy.
Solutions can blow up in finite time when the initial energy is negative. Blow-up requires negative initial energy. A growth inequality on F' is required. Blow-up occurs in the gradient L∞ norm. Positive energy yields global existence. Blow-up may occur even for small initial data.
